key_insight: A symmetry-based framework predicts where spin splitting, weak ferromagnetic canting, and anomalous Hall transport appear in orthorhombic Pbnm altermagnetic perovskites from the magnetic order alone.
engineering_relevance: These design rules can guide the selection and tuning of perovskite oxides for low-net-magnetization spintronic and Hall-transport devices.
method: Combined spin and magnetic group theory with first-principles calculations.
Mapped magnetic irreducible representations to spin-splitting planes, effective Hamiltonians, canting directions, and allowed AHC tensor components.
Validated the symmetry predictions across eight experimentally realized orthorhombic perovskite oxides.
evidence_signal: The framework was tested on eight materials spanning insulating and metallic regimes, including LaTiO3 and CaCrO3 with anomalous Hall conductivities of about 38 and 205 S/cm.
watch_item: The predicted Hall response depends on symmetry-protected band crossings and SOC-induced gaps, so disorder, strain, or structural deviations from ideal Pbnm symmetry could reduce the effect.
paper_title: Symmetry-guided Design Principles for Spin Splitting and Hall Transport in Orthorhombic Altermagnetic Perovskites
